findings.evidence: Fig 7.7, PDF p. 160: "in-flight ≈ KV budget ÷ KV per request | ≈ 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB ≈ 17.5 → ~17 requests" | Ch 4, PDF p. 90: "Requests in flight ≠ KV-resident sequences. A request in the queue, or one whose prefill is not yet admitted, is 'in flight' from the user's perspective but does not yet hold a KV slot. In-flight concurrency upper-bounds the KV-concurrency the system must serve, but the KV budget is sized by the number of resident active sequences"
findings.issue: The figure labels the KV-slot count as 'in-flight' and equates it with KV-budget ÷ KV-per-request. Ch 4 makes the opposite distinction a named common mistake and states that the KV budget is sized by resident sequences, not by in-flight requests. The label therefore uses, in the one diagram a reader is most likely to screenshot, precisely the term the book warns is wrong; the same distinction is silently respected in Ch 17's ⌈344/17⌉ screen, where 344 is the Little's-Law in-flight figure being divided by resident-slot capacity.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the Fig 7.7 quantity as 'KV-resident slots (concurrent sequences)' and, if the in-flight relation is worth showing, add a second, clearly distinguished row stating that in-flight requests ≥ resident slots (queued requests hold no KV slot), cross-referencing Ch 4 §4.3.

findings.evidence: PDF p. 140: "3×H100 total VRAM | 240 GB | [DERIVED] 165 GB < 240 GB | fits 3×H100 at 9.2K? | passes aggregate bytes only; TP=3 placement not established | 164.1 GB < 240 GB, but tensor parallelism shards attention heads, not the hidden dim ..." — while the two adjacent rows read "2×H100 total VRAM | 160 GB | [1P: NVIDIA H100 spec]" and "8×H100 total VRAM | 640 GB | [1P: NVIDIA H100 spec]"
findings.issue: The 'Derivation' cell for the 3×H100 row does not derive the value 240 GB — it states a fit comparison ('165 GB < 240 GB') that is then repeated verbatim in the 'fits 3×H100 at 9.2K?' row, where the 165 GB should be 164.1 GB to match the other rows' basis. The label is also inconsistent with its siblings: 2×H100 (160 GB) and 8×H100 (640 GB) are equally products of the vendor constant (80 GB) but are tagged [1P: NVIDIA H100 spec], while 3×H100 (240 GB) is tagged bare [DERIVED] with no Axis-1 provenance, contrary to the Preface's rule that a value computed from a first-party constant is [1P][DERIVED].
findings.fix_instruction: Change the derivation cell to '3 × 80 GB [1P][DERIVED]' (or '[1P: NVIDIA H100 spec] × 3'), tag it [1P][DERIVED] to match the sibling rows' provenance, and remove the duplicated fit comparison — it belongs only in the 'fits 3×H100 at 9.2K?' row, where it should read 164.1 GB < 240 GB for consistency with the 2×H100 and 8×H100 rows.

findings.chapter: Ch 7 (Memory Is the First Constraint), §7.8 mini-case
findings.evidence: p.161: premise 'We need to let all 5,000 employees ask questions over our internal wikis.' followed by 'The next step — turning "5,000 employees" into ~2,000 registered users, ~100 concurrent typical / ~400 at peak, ~10 requests/s [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION, from Ch 4 Table 4-2]'. Ch 4's mini-case (p.102-103) treats the same 5,000-employee headcount as a distinct growth scenario: 'Note this mini-case is a 5,000-employee growth scenario at 50 rps, distinct from the canonical 40 rps peak (which sizes to ~21 hosts full-util...)'.
findings.issue: Scenario bookkeeping contradiction: the identical '5,000 employees' ask is mapped here onto the canonical 2,000-user / 10-rps workload, while Ch 4 explicitly sizes 5,000 employees as a separate 50-rps / 26–40-host case; 5,000 cannot be 'turned into' 2,000 registered users.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-anchor the ask to a vague population (as Ch 1's mini-case does: 'thousands of employees'), or state that the canonical 2,000-user scenario is adopted as a modeling assumption despite the larger headcount, flagging the delta.

findings.chapter: Ch 7 (Memory Is the First Constraint), Table 7-1 'fits 3×H100 at 9.2K?' note
findings.evidence: p.140: 'the canonical 64-query-head / 8-KV-head geometry does not partition evenly into 3 ranks (64/3 = 21.3, 8/3 = 2.7…)'. The canonical teaching model is full-MHA — Table 4-2 (p.86): 'full-MHA reference model (K/V width = hidden_dim)… every query head keeps its own K,V'; Ch 7 itself (p.141-142): 'n_KV-heads = n_query-heads' for full MHA, and '8 KV-heads' is attributed to the GQA example ('LLaMA-2 70B… has 64 query heads but only 8 KV-heads').
findings.issue: Geometry mislabeled: the canonical full-MHA model has 64 KV heads (K/V width = hidden dim), not 8; the 64Q/8KV split belongs to the GQA sensitivity example. The 3-rank divisibility conclusion still holds (64/64 also fails), but the attribution is wrong.
findings.fix_instruction: Reword to 'the canonical 64-query-head full-MHA geometry (and the GQA variant's 64/8 head split alike) does not partition evenly into 3 ranks', or cite the GQA/LLaMA-2 example explicitly.
